These outcomes favor distinct nitrogen-environment curves. For alcohols, the m205 plateau hypothesis is rejected: at the same 49.5 mg loading, measured endpoints increased from 10.51/25.36 mL at 1/1 to 54.52/89.72 mL at 5/1. m119 and m99 also required substantial upward acquisition-time corrections at 5/1, while m60's 10/1 prediction was close. Loading therefore remains worth testing selectively, without assigning every miss to sample amount. An evidence-identity correction is essential: the observed table assigns 904fa4a17e429d0616f5 to m193 at 0/1, not to the m81 low-load 5/1 experiment described in its earlier reason. I do not treat that record as m81 evidence; the eligible 55.5 mg m81 experiment is selected now. The m76 lower-load and 2/1 results and m93 1/1 result all showed early elution, weakening analog transfer of the exceptional m76 observation. m73 remains an unresolved separate case, motivating a targeted near-repeat and local contrasts. Finally, m94's large underprediction and m166/m167's overpredictions further weaken a blanket acceptor-rich upward correction. All error statements here refer to acquisition-time predictions, not current-model residuals.","batch_rationale":"The batch uses local experiments where their contrasts can teach relationships that single large-error labels cannot. Nitrogen curve extensions test transfer after errors of opposite signs. Alcohol pairs explore donor environment, while matched loading comparisons and the m205 two-ratio/two-amount grid test selective use of the loading feature. The m125 and m173 experiments examine recorded injection volume without inventing concentration, flow or other absent variables. Three m73 experiments address reproducibility and locality of an observation that could otherwise influence a large ester family. Carbonyl curve gaps and extrapolation checks repair known transfer weaknesses, and matched novel-scaffold pairs add useful coverage of ring geometry, conjugation and combined ether/ester functionality. Moderate-retention and predicted-flat curves provide discriminating controls alongside steep-response cases. Duplicate catalog rows are avoided except for the deliberately justified m73 near-repeat. These labels should improve endpoint-specific structure-condition representations across the Row-distribution, while allowing some unusual observations to remain unexplained when recorded variables are insufficient."}
